steps.beforeInstructorMessage: An open-ended straight draw (OESD) has 8 outs—you can hit on either end of the straight. Same idea as the flush draw: use the rule of 4 on the flop (two cards to come). Fewer outs than a flush draw means less equity, so you need better pot odds (or implied odds) to call with an OESD than with a flush draw.
steps.question: What approximate equity does an 8-out straight draw have by the river?
steps.followUpInstructorMessage: When ready, continue to the question.

steps.beforeInstructorMessage: You have an open-ended straight draw on the flop (8 outs). You will see both the turn and the river.
steps.question: Approximately what is your chance to make the straight by the river?

gradingSpecJson.responseCorrect: Correct. 8 outs × 4 = 32% by the river. So an OESD has a bit less equity than a flush draw (36%); you need good pot odds or implied odds to call with it.
gradingSpecJson.responseIncorrect: Not quite. Rule of 4: on the flop with two cards to come, 8 outs × 4 = 32% chance to hit by the river.
gradingSpecJson.followUpContent: On the flop with two cards to come: 8 outs × 4 = 32%. An open-ended straight draw has 8 outs (four cards on each end of the straight). Use the rule of 2 for one card to come: 8 × 2 = 16%. Poker IQ: OESD (32%) is weaker than a flush draw (36%), so you need at least 3:1 (25% needed) to call in a vacuum, and at 2:1 (33%) you're slightly short—look for implied odds or fold. Knowing both your equity and the break-even % is how you stop calling or folding by feel.
